requirements.wording: Policy Assessments Purpose A requirement of the Joint Accreditation System of Australia & New Zealand (JASANZ) under which the Quality and Safety Program (QSPP) is accredited is to use an allocation model for assessments. To achieve this, QSPP has partnered with Ernst and Young (EY). Assessments are conducted by QSPP endorsed assessors that have been drawn from EY’s specialist audit practice. This policy describes principles guiding the administration of QSPP assessments. 1. Application EY will allocate a QSPP endorsed assessor to conduct a QSPP assessment. Assessment services are administered by EY, QSPP’s assessment partner. EY will allocate a QSPP endorsed assessor based on the agreed assessment date and available assessor resources. A pharmacy is not able to request a specific assessor. For pharmacies requesting an initial assessment it may take up to six months for an assessment date to become available. 1.1 Alternate assessor requests Consistent with the QSPP Program Rules, where a real or perceived possibility of a conflict of interest (‘conflict’) has been confirmed, QSPP will assess the alleged conflict. If considered a conflict, QSPP will arrange for another QSPP endorsed assessor to conduct the assessment as per the QSPP assessor allocation process. 1.2 Witnessed assessments Consistent with the Program Rules an additional attendee may be present at the time of assessment. This person is there to witness the assessment process and has no impact on the assessment outcome. Where reasonable, QSPP will provide advance notice of an additional attendee. 2. Cancelled assessments 2.1 Cancellation or changes less than 10 calendar days Should an assessment date booking be changed or cancelled by a pharmacy owner or authorised delegate with less than 10 calendar days’ notice, a pharmacy will: 1. forfeit their QSPP Assessment included as part of the QSPP Annual Fee, or 2. a cancellation fee equivalent to the current assessment fee (see schedule of fees), will be charged, and 3. any travel expenses incurred to date by the assessment company will be charged. An assessment may also be cancelled at the discretion of QSPP where it is apparent that a pharmacy is not in a position to proceed with assessment e.g. at least one pharmacy owner not being present or lack of preparedness. In such instances points 1 to 3 above would also apply. requirements.wording: Policy Exceptional Circumstances Purpose The purpose of this policy is to support QSPP Program Rules and describe circumstances under which an application for extension or permanent change will be considered for an assessment date, a corrective action due date to address a minor non-conformance, or an accreditation expiry date. Scope Any application for reschedule, extension or permanent date change must be made prior to the corrective action due date or accreditation expiry date. All pharmacies should be ready to be assessed under the program at any point, and therefore variations to the confirmed assessment date can only be granted in exceptional circumstances. Exceptional circumstances are considered to be unavoidable or unforeseen events that have an immediate impact in the pharmacy’s ability to deliver regular services and where the pharmacy has done all reasonable action to mitigate impact to maintain their accreditation (out of the pharmacy’s control). Examples of exceptional circumstances may include, but are not limited to: • recent burglary or severe unexpected damage to premises, e.g. fire, flood • bereavement of immediate family member • unforeseen significant medical emergencies • natural disasters. Consideration may also be provided where the pharmacy is moving location or a sale of a pharmacy, depending on impact to business operations. Reasonable requests for additional time which are not considered exceptional circumstances will be considered based on resources available at the time. All applications should include the provision of detailed information and evidence to support the request. Accreditation expiry date extension and assessment date reschedule requests A pharmacy may request an accreditation expiry date extension of no more than three calendar months. This request must be received prior to the pharmacy’s existing accreditation expiry date. The request will only be granted in exceptional circumstances. A pharmacy may also request an assessment date reschedule in instances where moving the assessment date will not impact the pharmacy from completing all assessment activities prior to the accreditation expiry date. As with extension requests, these requests will only be granted in exceptional circumstances. requirements.wording: Policy Sanctions Management Purpose The purpose of this Policy is to establish a clear, consistent and fair framework for managing non‑compliance with the requirements of the Quality and Safety Pharmacy Program (QSPP). This Policy aims to: • Protect the integrity, credibility and reputation of QSPP • Safeguard patient safety and public confidence • Promote continuous quality improvement by participating pharmacies • Ensure sanctions are applied proportionately, consistently and transparently • Embed procedural fairness (natural justice) in all compliance and enforcement actions. Context This Policy applies to: • All pharmacies participating in QSPP • All alleged or identified non‑compliance with QSPP Program Rules, Standards, User Assessment Guide, Terms and Conditions, or applicable legislation. • Any occasion where QSPP may consider or is considering imposing a form of sanction. Guiding Principles All sanctions and enforcement actions under QSPP will be guided by the following principles: Procedural Fairness (Natural Justice) QSPP will ensure that: • Pharmacy owner/s are clearly informed of alleged non-compliance • Relevant evidence is disclosed, subject to confidentiality obligations • Pharmacy owner/s are given a reasonable opportunity to respond • Decisions are made by an impartial and appropriately authorised decision‑maker • Decisions are documented with clear reasons • Appealable decisions are subject to independent review. Proportionality Sanctions will be proportionate to: • The seriousness of the non‑compliance • The level of risk to patient safety • Whether the issue is isolated or systemic • The pharmacy’s compliance history.
